name: churn-prevention
description: Five skills for subscription churn, each computed from your own data. Start from "customers keep cancelling": split failed payments from chosen cancellations and see which to fix first. Audit a cancel flow against 16 checks and dated cancellation rules for the US (federal and California), the EU and the UK; judge a save offer by who still pays after the discount ends, against a holdout; sort failed payments by decline code into never retry, customer must act, and retry within card-network caps; test churn signals on your own history for lift, coverage and lead time; plan a consent-checked win-back for cancelled subscriptions. Reads what you paste, quotes no benchmarks, and never makes cancelling harder. Not legal advice.

interface.shortDescription: Cancel flows, save offers, failed payments, win-back
interface.longDescription: Five skills for keeping subscribers, each built on arithmetic you can recompute. A cancellation discount that looks like a 25.0% save rate (90 of 360 accepted) can turn out, measured in the first full-price month against a holdout, to be 15.0% vs 10.0%, a difference of 5.0 points with a 95% interval from -8.5 to +12.3: not established. Cancel-flow audit checks a flow against 16 checks and dated rules for the US (federal and California), the EU (including Germany and the EU withdrawal function) and the UK, and gives a redesign with one offer beside a visible cancel control. Save-offer economics separates acceptance, still paying after the discount, and gain over a holdout, with pause outcomes and cost per extra retained customer. Dunning plan is also the starting point for "customers keep cancelling": it splits failed payments from chosen cancellations. It sorts declines into never retry, customer must act, and wait-and-retry classes, checks retries against card-network limits and covers app-store grace periods. Churn signals tests which signals came before cancellations, with lift, recall, lead time and a leakage check. Win-back plan segments cancelled subscribers after consent checks and plans a holdout to measure the result. No benchmarks, no legal advice, and requests to make cancelling harder are declined.
defaultPrompt: Audit my cancel flow: Settings > Plan > required survey > 50% off 'expires if you leave' > chat with support to finish.
Save offer, $50 plan: 360 saw it, 90 took 30% off for 3 months, 54 paid full price in month 4. Holdout 40: 4 paying. Worth it?
500 accounts, 60 cancelled. Seats removed fired on 50 (20 cancelled, 41 days ahead); export on 30 (18, 2 days). Act on which?
